node.label: Jürgen Habermas
node.date_label: Strukturwandel der Öffentlichkeit (1962) · “The Public Sphere”: original encyclopedia article (1964) · “The Public Sphere”: English translation (1974) · Theorie des kommunikativen Handelns (1981) · The Structural Transformation of the Public Sphere: English translation (1989)
node.description: Distinguishes the public sphere of discussion from state authority and asks how communication can subject power to criticism. The encyclopedia article’s model of access is a normative problem rather than proof that historical bourgeois publics were inclusive. Its closing discussion leaves room for accountable organized communication rather than an inevitable narrative of complete decline. Nancy Fraser’s named 1990 criticism contests the bracketing of inequality and the assumption of one comprehensive public, while retaining the importance of publicity for democracy. The entry distinguishes this specifically attributed critique from a shared position of all feminist or gender historians.

proposed_edges.relationship: Develops publicity as discussion distinct from state authority, with accountability as a problem for organized communication.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Reuses retained complete primary article review, pp. 49–55 and notes 1–6. Ideal access does not establish empirical equality, and the final page does not require inevitable total decline.

proposed_edges.relationship: Nancy Fraser challenges the exclusionary assumptions of the bourgeois-public model and distinguishes counterpublics and decision-making publics.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Incoming edge locates Fraser’s specifically named 1990 intervention, not a consensus of gender historians. Reuses retained selected pp. 56–62, 67, 75–77 and stated fragments/notes. Note 9 acknowledges Habermas knew alternative publics; counterpublics can themselves exclude.
